scope: Independent source-only review of v16-pinned segmented retry/unwind obstruction; no v3 implementation
verdict: Suitable to preserve as an obstruction and model. Do not adopt the uncompiled v2 deque prototype or claim unwind safety, production readiness or a speedup.
checks: Rechecked all six archive member hashes and exact author receipt; verified six v16 source inputs, immutable catalog and v2 patch git apply --check without applying the patch.

Independently modeled the three unexpired same-topic records with retries 0,4,2. Combined retry maxima are 5,5,5 and skip-refresh flags false,true,true; three separate batches yield maxima 1,5,3 and flags false,false,false.
Checked author model’s expired-first and 4096-capacity examples against source-derived expectations; reviewed source retry grouping, increment, expiry, first-index and backoff code.
Verified Tokio 1.53.3 pinned recv_many source hashes and cancel-safety documentation.
admission_fence: WorkerAdmission::close serializes on the commit mutex and flips accepting false before releasing it; production WorkerHandle try_send and previously reserved WorkerPermit::send check acceptance under that same mutex. Thus these handle paths cannot commit a new record after close returns. Raw senders used by tests can bypass the fence; no concurrent execution was performed.
other_source_findings: V16 closed-worker cleanup retires sticky state and releases the entire combined queued batch byte budget before its per-record callbacks; segmented cleanup can change callback-time observations.

Reserve before creating receiving.drain can preserve the scratch on a reservation panic, but reattachment during Drop and existing retry_sync topic-group allocation remain separate hazards. Split singleton reserve-before-pop addresses another conditional unwind window also present in v16.

A source-only repeated-scan fallback still needs access to all records; Tokio mpsc cannot be assumed to offer repeatable in-place channel iteration, so the post-close channel must first be retained in bounded storage or its representation redesigned.

Channel refills between a successful receive and admission closure can make scratch and the channel each contain up to the channel capacity; per-worker preallocation impacts memory and does not supply a global bound.
limitations: The Python models approximate selected source operations; no Rust, Tokio scheduling, allocation panic, callbacks, Kafka or benchmark was executed.
v2 patch was checked for applicability only, not integrated or compiled; its normal and error paths remain unqualified.
No root-cause conclusion for the hosted retained-backing failure and no production or performance claim.
